newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Bosnia wants more time for vote in Slovenia.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia wants more time for vote in Slovenia.

text.p: Bosnia's embassy in Slovenia complained on Thursday that all refugees in the country were unable to vote in Bosnia's first post-war election but poll organisers said the vast majority had cast a ballot.

"We suggested that elections (in Slovenia) be prolonged as about one quarter of registered voters did not receive ballots which should have been mailed to them," Bosnian embassy spokesman Ferhat Seta told Reuters.
Seta said the embassy estimated there were 40,000 Bosnian voters in Slovenia, of which most failed to register because of the complicated registry forms.

But the Ljubljana office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), the body in charge of running the polls, said it had received a vote from 12,300 people out of the 15,000 registered voters.

"The participation was 82.6 percent and we have seen no problems. The decision whether elections should be prolonged has to be made by the OSCE in Sarajevo," Vida Koren-Holm, the head of the Slovenian OSCE office, said.
Tens of thousands of Bosnian refugees in scores of host countries have been sending in postal votes for the Bosnian elections, which take place on September 14.
